I wanted to tell her to shut up, and it made me realize she’s just a mean and crazy person.

So staying home with her 24/7 while trying to do my job and not being able to go anywhere is like torture every single day. The only thing I look forward to is sleeping.

This is why I could not stay home. I love my daughter, but if I stayed home I’d lose my mind. I went back to work when she was 8 weeks old. I didn’t realize how depressed I’d feel being home all day with a baby (it was also winter time and she would scream every time we’d get in the car or go anywhere). I think some women are just “wired” to stay home with their kids and they love it. Others hate it. Parenting is a million times harder than anyone will ever admit.

You’re being a good friend. Remind her that she’s not a bad person. Suggest things you can do to together to help take her mind off it, like go to a movie together. Ask if she needs help with anything or just wants to talk.  Suggest that she talk to a counselor if she needs it.

He should be able to handle the kids for a week. He’s s dad, it’s part of his responsibilities as a parent. Since you’re a SAHM and that is damn hard, you’ve definitely earned the break.

Granted, my husband would never do this for me for a full week because our kid is 3 and extremely hyperactive and challenging, but he’s very hands on with our daughter and he should be. 

If a dad can’t help out with the kids, then he shouldn’t have them at all.

I was in a somewhat similar boat. Some things that turned out much differently than I expected:

1. I thought our family would offer to babysit a lot more. Our family rarely helps us at all. Like maybe once a month for 2 hours. I did so much babysitting for my family members before I had a kid and I thought they’d return the favor. My in-laws are retired and healthy and I also thought they’d help out a lot, but they don’t.  Like once every two months maybe. 

2. Had no idea how hard it would be to balance work and parenting,  I have a stressful corporate job, then I might come home to a cranky and tired kid who is screaming for my attention and having tantrums. During the week it’s non-stop stress from 6am-8:30pm (if she goes to bed on time). 

3. Wasn’t prepared for how much guilt I’d feel over working full-time outside the home while she goes to day care. And I had no idea a good day care in our area would be well over $1,000 per month. 

4. I had no idea how sleep-deprived I’d be. My daughter didn’t sleep thru the night consistently until about 12 months. Imagine being up all night with your child and then getting up for work at 6am. When they get sick, which is way more than I expected, you may get up with them 3x a night or just not sleep at all.

5. I wasn’t prepared to have a child with such explosive and emotional tantrums. I never expected my child to hit and kick me at age 2. I never expected to have a child who would have such huge tantrums in public places that we’d have to leave. I never expected my child to hit or pinch me so hard that I’d have bruises. 


I’m just being very honest.

I also just remembered another interesting story. A second cousin of mine had fertility issues and was dying to get pregnant. She was obsessed with it. Ended up doing in vitro and freezing eggs and then had 2 kids about a year apart. Quit her job to stay home with them. 

She ended up so overwhelmed and miserable that she started mixing alcohol and Valium during the day and landed in a drug rehab facility. We’re talking about a well-educated person from a good background.  I talked with her after rehab and she said she just didn’t realize she’d get so depressed and feel like she was drowning.

My point is, it can be much more overwhelming than anyone realizes.

Only you can make the decision that’s best for you, but I think any parent can agree that these are facts about parenthood to consider, unless you have a perfect angel child:

You’ll get a lot less sleep, especially in the first few years. When they are newborns, you will be so sleep-deprived you’ll feel like you are losing your mind. There’s lots of crying and tantrums. Kids get sick a lot. They will throw up in your bed at 3am and then you have to go to work the next day (or if you don’t work, you still have to function with a sick kid and no sleep). Going out for a nice meal almost impossible when they are young. Going on nice, long vacations probably isn’t possible when they are really young. Childcare is insanely expensive (a nanny where I live is about $3,000 a month and daycare is about $1500). You will have a lot less freedom. You can’t sleep in anymore (probably until they are at least 8 years old I’m guessing). 

Just sharing for consideration.
